Consult Summary:
- Acute new unilateral left-sided headache with blurred vision (zigzag lines), dizziness, nausea/vomiting beginning this morning with sudden onset. Clinician suspects migraine; no focal neurological deficits reported. Plan includes NSAID and antiemetic, hydration, and referral for same-day neurological assessment if symptoms persist; patient advised to minimize screen exposure and to contact clinic if symptoms worsen or resolve.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute left-sided headache with visual disturbances starting this morning (sudden onset); pain described as significant (6/10 relative to prior kidney stone), one-sided (left) with movement-induced worsening.
- Associated symptoms: blurred vision with zigzag lines, nausea, vomiting, dizziness; unable to tolerate screens; no reported weakness or gait abnormalities.
- Systems review: Visual disturbance and nausea/vomiting positive; no focal neurological symptoms reported (no limb weakness, no ataxia).
- Social history/Medications/Examination findings:
  - Regular medications: none reported.
  - Allergies: none reported.
  - Pregnancy: not pregnant (patient expressed doubt about pregnancy; no test documented).
  - Examination findings (per clinician): no neurological deficits observed; patient able to walk; no focal deficits noted; headache localized to left side.
- Impression: Migraine suspected (first presentation).

Issue 2:
- Past Medical History: Kidney stones (history of stones).
- Family history: Mother with migraines; mother also has hypothyroidism; conflicting mention of thyroid disease (initially hypothyroidism in family; clinician noted hyperthyroid then clarified hypothyroidism again); conflict noted.
- Medications/Allergies: No regular medications; no known drug allergies.
- Social History: Not documented beyond stated medical history.
- Relevant examination findings: None beyond patient-reported symptoms; no weakness or focal deficits.
- Differential considerations: Patient expressed concern for serious etiologies (brain tumor or stroke); however currently no focal deficits and presentation favors migraine.

Issue 3:
- Plan and management:
  - Pharmacologic: Recommend ibuprofen for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented); antiemetic (dose/route/frequency not documented); consider anti-sickness medication as part of migraine treatment (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Adjunct measures: Recommend sugary, carbonated drinks (e.g., Coca-Cola) as part of interim management; advise minimizing screen exposure.
  - Contingency plan: If migraine resolves, appointment can be canceled; otherwise proceed to same-day neurological assessment to perform a full neurological exam.
  - Follow-up: Schedule same-day assessment; contact clinic if symptoms worsen or significantly improve before the appointment.
  - Education/Verbal: Patient acknowledged plan and felt it was reasonable.

Medications:
- Paracetamol (taken by patient; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Ibuprofen (recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Anti-sickness/antiemetic (not specified; dose/route/frequency not documented)

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Kidney stones (past)

Social History:
- Not otherwise documented (no regular medications; not pregnant)

Preventative History:
- Not documented

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented
- Findings: No neurological deficits reported; patient able to walk; left-sided headache; visual disturbances (blurred vision with zigzag lines); nausea/vomiting; worsened with movement. No weakness or gait abnormalities noted.

Plan:
- Initiate self-management for migraine with ibuprofen and antiemetic; consider ginger/antiemetic options as appropriate (not specified).
- Hydration and intake of sugary carbonated beverage (e.g., Coke) as adjunct.
- Avoid or minimize screen exposure during acute period.
- Arrange same-day neurological assessment for a full exam if symptoms persist or worsen.
- If symptoms improve, cancellation of the appointment is acceptable; contact the clinic if needed.
- Monitor for red flags and seek urgent care if new neurological deficits develop or symptoms worsen.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs and full physical examination documentation (no vitals; limited exam notes).
  - Medication doses, routes, and frequencies for ibuprofen and antiemetic not provided.
  - Comprehensive med reconciliation and allergy verification beyond “no known allergies.”
  - Preventive health history (cervical screening, mammography, PSA, FIT/FOBT, bone density, vaccinations) not documented.
  - Social determinants (smoking status, alcohol use, living situation) not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Family thyroid disease history conflicting (hypothyroidism vs. hyperthyroidism mentioned; conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Brief connection drop during the interview; some parts were repetitive or partially inaudible, but core clinical details were captured.
